comparison.prefix_reasoning_summary: The code snippet for 'findElements' shows it only checks for '#', '.', and various pseudo-selectors. It does not check for '['. When a query like 'table[class~=x|y]' is processed, the parser reaches the attribute part, but 'findElements' doesn't know how to handle '[', leading to the 'unhandled' exception.
comparison.postfix_reasoning_summary: The bug is a failure in the parsing algorithm used to extract sub-queries from a CSS selector string. The existing implementation used a simple 'consumeToAny' which is not context-aware regarding nested structures (like attribute selectors). This is a classic algorithmic deficiency in handling complex input strings.

applicable_rules.condition: pre-fix sees symptoms only; post-fix sees the actual code change
applicable_rules.explanation: Pre-fix classification is based on observable symptoms (stack traces, failing tests, error messages) which often surface the effect rather than the root cause.  Post-fix classification has access to the diff showing exactly what changed, revealing the true nature of the fix.  Different evidence bases legitimately produce different classifications.
applicable_rules.literature: Kang et al. (2023) — AutoSD: evidence-dependent hypothesis generation

applicable_rules.condition: ODC boundary ambiguity between similar types
applicable_rules.explanation: The ODC taxonomy has known boundary ambiguity zones, especially between Algorithm/Method ↔ Checking, and Function/Class/Object ↔ Interface/O-O Messages.  Even expert human classifiers disagree on 20-30% of bugs (Chillarege 1992).  Cohen's Kappa of 0.6-0.8 is considered 'substantial' agreement in defect classification — not perfection.
applicable_rules.literature: Chillarege et al. (1992), Thung et al. (2012) — 77.8% ceiling
